description: NOVA's shipped nozzle and its exhaust plume at the shipped ambient: the station march from the exit plane and the correlated structure

notes: Marched 2.00 lip radii on 130 stations, stopping on maxLength. Worst mass continuity error -0.72 per cent of the exit mass flow.
A Mach disk stands 7.9 lip radii downstream by Ashkenas and Sherman. Nothing in this field represents it: the march is isentropic and carries no shock.
Marched 10.00 lip radii on 390 stations, stopping on maxLength. Worst mass continuity error -53.92 per cent of the exit mass flow.
That is past the 1.0 per cent this field is called trustworthy within, so the shape is drawable and the numbers on it are not. Shorten the reach.
A Mach disk stands 7.9 lip radii downstream by Ashkenas and Sherman. Nothing in this field represents it: the march is isentropic and carries no shock.

Nozzle pressure ratio 1379.0 is above the Mach disk onset threshold of 3.5, so the first cell is bounded by a Mach disk rather than a regular reflection. Published onset thresholds range from about 3.1 to 3.9, so treat the switch as soft.

Shock cell amplitude capped to keep the boundary off the axis. The correlated turning angle implies a swell wider than the lip radius, so the drawn boundary understates the plume; use it for cell spacing and scale, not for width.

Boundary, cell spacing and Mach disk are correlations (Prandtl 1904 / Pack, Ashkenas and Sherman 1966, Tam and Tanna); the interior of the plume is not solved. Cell spacing with Pack's coefficient would be 6.655 m against 7.124 m with Prandtl's, which is a fair measure of the uncertainty.
